claim: Muravyev & Pearson (Review of Financial Studies, 2020) find that effective spreads for traders who time their executions are under 40% of conventional measures, and the overall average effective spread is about one-quarter smaller than conventional estimates.

evidence.quote: Effective spreads of traders who time executions are less than 40% of the size of conventional measures, and the overall average effective spread is one-quarter smaller than conventional estimates.
Conventional measures of transactions costs are large: The effective spreads are about 80% of the size of the quoted spreads. The price impacts are also large.

claim: Early exercise of an in-the-money American call just before the ex-dividend date is rational when the call's remaining time (extrinsic) value is less than the dividend, so a short ITM call is at high assignment risk the day before ex-dividend under that condition.

evidence.quote: Time value must be less than the dividend for early exercise to make economic sense. Exercising forfeits remaining time value, so the dividend needs to exceed that amount.
if a trader is short an ITM call and the extrinsic value of the corresponding put is less than the upcoming dividend, the trader is more likely to be subject to early assignment
